BBC News (Ruth Comerford, BBC London) — published Sat 26 Sep 2026, 12:54 BST (11:54 GMT), updated 14:21 BST

HEADLINE: Met to re-examine CCTV footage from unsolved Jill Dando murder

The Met Police has confirmed it will re-examine CCTV footage relating to the unsolved murder of BBC presenter Jill Dando, 27 years ago. Dando was shot dead with a single bullet on her doorstep in Fulham in April 1999; despite one of the biggest and most high-profile murder investigations in British history, the case remains unsolved.

QUOTE (Met Police spokesperson): recent advancements in CCTV enhancement technology had "provided investigators with the opportunity to re-examine original footage from Putney Bridge train station".

The CCTV includes an unidentified man who was seen sprinting near the scene of the shooting, 20 minutes after the event. The Met said that in the 27 years since Dando's death the investigation had been "subject to numerous reviews", aiming to identify whether matters could be progressed with advances in technology and forensics. It warned this latest review was part of "ongoing inquiries and should not be interpreted as a significant line of inquiry nor as a new investigation being opened on this matter".

Dando was born in Weston-super-Mare, Somerset, worked for the BBC for 14 years and was 37 when she died on the doorstep of her home in Gowan Avenue. Barry George, a local man, was convicted of her murder and spent eight years in jail before being acquitted at a retrial in 2008.
